android.desc: Prana Breath is a breathing and meditation app with no narrator. Pick a practice, follow the animation, and breathe. 80+ breathing exercises and meditations, from Nadi Shodhana to 4-7-8 and box breathing. Free to start, no ads ever. Meditation you do, not meditation you listen to Most meditation apps are a recording of a stranger's voice. This one is not. It is a meditation timer that holds the structure for you: the pace, the stages and the interval bell. Behind it you choose what you hear, or choose nothing at all. If a voice in your ear makes it harder to settle, or if nobody narrates in your language, this is the app you were looking for. A library, not a playlist 80+ practices in 7 collections, from plain beginner breathwork to classical pranayama. Every one of them comes with a real explanation: what it does, how to sit, what can go wrong, and where it came from, with sources you can go and check. • Essentials: 12 short practices, free, for a first session today • Pranayama: 27 classical practices including Nadi Shodhana, Bhramari, Kapalabhati, Ujjayi, Bhastrika and Sitali • Breathing traditions: Sufi, Tibetan, Taoist and Orthodox practices, cited properly • Modern methods: coherent breathing, 4-7-8, box breathing, Buteyko, cyclic hyperventilation • Applied methods: for singers, divers, runners, and anyone who needs steady hands • Habits: for cravings, for the evening snack, for the cigarette you did not want • Health metrics: 10 measurements you take yourself and follow over months What a few minutes a day is good for A slow, even breath settles the nervous system and takes the edge off a tense day. A long exhale is one of the few things you can actually do about anxiety in the moment, anywhere, without anyone noticing. Regular practice sharpens attention, works the muscles that do the breathing so they tire less, and supports the body in the same ordinary way that walking, sleep and cold water do. Some patterns wake you up, some slow you down toward sleep, and the app tells you which is which. Sound, and how much of it 34 backgrounds: nightingale, cuckoo, owl, gull, a crackling fire, Tibetan and Vajrayana chanting. A separate sound marks every phase of the breath, so you can put the phone face down, close your eyes and follow the whole session by ear. Or run it in silence.
